name: Manganese
mobility: IMMOBILE (deficiency on YOUNGER leaves, but interveinal with more diffuse/greyish tone than Fe)

overview.whyImportant: Manganese activates the water-splitting step of photosynthesis (oxygen evolution) and many enzymes. Deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis of younger leaves with grey/brown flecks; common on high-pH, sandy and heavily-limed soils.

plantFunctions.roleInsidePlant: Activates photosynthetic oxygen-evolving complex, enzymes of respiration and N metabolism.
plantFunctions.chlorophyllFormation: Needed for chlorophyll and photosystem function.
plantFunctions.yieldContribution: Sustains photosynthesis; deficiency reduces yield, esp. cereals/legumes on high-pH soils.

whyDeficiencyHappens.why: Mn oxidises to unavailable forms above pH ~6.5 — main cause.
Rarely deficient (often toxic in very acid soils).

whyDeficiencyHappens.condition: Nutrient imbalance / excess Fe, Zn, Cu, high P

whyDeficiencyHappens.why: Raises pH, oxidises Mn to unavailable forms.
Immobile Mn needs active root foraging.
Over-liming and ignoring Mn on alkaline soils.

symptoms.note: Mn IMMOBILE — younger leaves affected; interveinal chlorosis with GREYISH tone and brown flecks/necrotic spots (finer, more diffuse than Fe).
symptoms.early: Younger leaves pale interveinal, veins green (broader green band than Fe).
symptoms.middle: Interveinal yellowing with grey/brown flecks/streaks; 'grey speck' in cereals.
symptoms.severe: Necrotic interveinal streaks, poor growth; in legumes 'marsh spot' in seeds.
symptoms.youngLeaves: First affected: interveinal chlorosis + brown/grey flecking.
symptoms.wholePlant: Younger canopy interveinal-chlorotic with brown flecks, reduced vigour on high-pH soils.

cropWiseSymptoms.symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis with brown flecks on younger leaves on alkaline soils.
Interveinal yellowing of young leaves, brown flecks; on high-pH soils.
Interveinal chlorosis + specks on younger leaves.
Young-leaf interveinal mottling in high-pH conditions.
Interveinal chlorosis with flecks on young leaves.
Interveinal chlorosis of young leaves, netted pattern.
Interveinal chlorosis with flecking on young leaves.
Interveinal chlorosis/olive-grey streaks on younger leaves on alkaline soils.
Grey interveinal streaks on young leaves (sandy alkaline soils).
Interveinal chlorosis + possible marsh spot in seed.
Young-leaf interveinal chlorosis on high-pH soils.
Interveinal chlorosis with streaks on younger leaves on alkaline soils.

howToFix.soilApplicationDose: 8-10 kg/acre (with FYM; less efficient on high pH)
howToFix.methodOfApplication: FOLIAR most effective on alkaline soils; repeat
howToFix.precautions: Soil Mn quickly oxidised on high-pH soils — prefer foliar; don't over-lime.

methodOfApplication.broadcast: Soil MnSO4 with FYM (limited on high pH).
methodOfApplication.bandPlacement: Banded MnSO4 near roots is better than broadcast on alkaline soils.
methodOfApplication.foliarSpray: 0.5% MnSO4 (+0.5% urea) — the reliable fix on alkaline soils; repeat.
methodOfApplication.seedTreatment: MnSO4 seed treatment used in some cereals/pulses on deficient soils.

toxicity.whatHappens: Mn toxicity on very ACID soils (pH <5.5).
toxicity.plantToxicitySymptoms: Brown spots on older leaves, crinkling, stunting; interveinal in some crops.
toxicity.correctionMethods: Lime acid soils to raise pH; improve drainage; balance with Fe.

faq.q: Mn aur Fe deficiency me farak?
